title: p95 drift sentinel for dedicated cluster stability
creator: Ayesha Kumar
description: Build a lightweight "p95 drift sentinel" that runs alongside the existing dedicated-capacity soak harness to catch small-but-persistent latency regressions that only appear after prolonged steady-state or repeated burst cycles. Motivation: some regressions don’t show as immediate failures but manifest as a rising p95 over days (tokens/sec drop, KV cache warmup variance, kernel selection mismatches). The sentinel will: 1) compute per-route rolling p95 with configurable windows (1h/6h/24h), 2) compare against a baseline profile (golden run) using relative delta and statistical significance heuristics, 3) correlate token/sec and request-rate changes, 4) flag anomalies that coincide with autoscaler events (scale-ups/scale-downs) and cache-eviction boundaries, and 5) emit structured findings (summary + traces + representative request ids) to the console telemetry and an alerting channel for on-call triage. Implementation constraints: keep runtime overhead <1% of main harness; avoid excessive retention of raw latencies (only store sketches/quantile-reservoirs), support both burst and steady-state phases, and integrate with current soak driver so runs can be scheduled daily or attached to CI-release gates.
acceptance_criteria: Sentinel computes rolling p95 per-route and per-model with configurable windows and returns time-series compatible with existing dashboards
Alerts are produced when relative p95 delta > 10% over a 24h window and confirmed by a 6h rolling-significance test
Alert payload includes tokens/sec, request-rate, autoscaler events in that window, and top-5 representative traces
End-to-end run of the sentinel on a dedicated soak cluster shows <1% CPU overhead and <5% memory overhead compared to baseline harness
Synthetic regression injected (latency +15% at tail) is detected within the configured window and creates a ticket with attached artifacts
